blocks.title: Gas exchange
blocks.md: **Gas exchange** is the diffusion of oxygen into the blood and carbon dioxide out of it. It takes place in the **alveoli** of the lungs. Air passes through the nose, **trachea** (held open by rings of cartilage), **bronchi** and **bronchioles** to the alveoli. The **ciliated cells** and **mucus** of the airways trap dust and microbes.

blocks.caption: One alveolus and its capillary.
blocks.alt: An alveolus drawn as a circle containing air next to a blood capillary: oxygen diffuses into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out; the wall is one cell thick.

blocks.title: Adaptations of alveoli
blocks.md:
- Very **large total surface area** (millions of alveoli).
- **Thin walls** (one cell thick) so the diffusion distance is short.
- A rich network of **capillaries** that carries oxygen away and brings carbon dioxide, keeping the concentration gradient steep.
- A **moist** lining in which gases dissolve.
- Fresh air from **ventilation** keeps a high oxygen concentration.

blocks.title: Mechanism of breathing
blocks.md:
**Inhalation**: intercostal muscles contract and raise the ribs up and out; the **diaphragm** contracts and flattens; the volume of the chest increases, the pressure falls and air enters.

**Exhalation**: the intercostal muscles and diaphragm relax; the ribs fall and the diaphragm rises; the volume decreases, the pressure rises and air is forced out.

blocks.caption: Approximate composition of inhaled and exhaled air.
blocks.alt: A bar chart: oxygen about 21 percent in and 16 percent out; carbon dioxide about 0.04 percent in and 4 percent out.

blocks.title: Smoking and health (flag for health review)
blocks.md: Tobacco smoke contains **tar** (which damages the airways and can cause lung cancer), **nicotine** (an addictive drug), and **carbon monoxide**, which combines with haemoglobin and reduces the oxygen carried. Smoking is linked with bronchitis, emphysema and heart disease. Stopping smoking improves health; seek advice from a health worker.

blocks.title: Volume of air breathed per minute
blocks.statement: A resting boy takes 16 breaths per minute and inhales about 500 cm³ of air with each breath. Calculate the volume of air breathed per minute.
steps: Volume per minute = volume per breath × breaths per minute.

blocks.title: Limewater test
blocks.statement: Exhaled air is bubbled through limewater and it turns milky. Air from a pump does so only after a long time. What does this show?
steps: Limewater turns milky in the presence of carbon dioxide.
Exhaled air has more carbon dioxide than inhaled air.
blocks.answer: Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air.

blocks.title: Respiration
blocks.md:
**Respiration** is the chemical process in living cells that releases **energy from food** (usually glucose). Energy is used for muscle contraction, growth, active transport, making proteins and keeping a constant body temperature.

**Aerobic respiration** uses oxygen. It takes place in the **mitochondria**.

blocks.title: Anaerobic respiration
blocks.md:
**Anaerobic respiration** releases energy from glucose **without oxygen**. It releases much *less* energy per glucose molecule.

- In **muscles** (hard exercise): glucose → **lactic acid** + a little energy.
- In **yeast** (fermentation): glucose → **ethanol** + **carbon dioxide** + a little energy.

Yeast fermentation is used to make bread (CO₂ makes dough rise), palm wine and beer.

blocks.caption: Aerobic and anaerobic (muscle) respiration.
blocks.alt: Two rows of boxes: glucose plus oxygen gives energy with carbon dioxide and water; and glucose gives lactic acid with only a little energy in muscles.

blocks.title: Oxygen debt
blocks.md: During sprinting the muscles respire anaerobically and **lactic acid** builds up, causing fatigue. After the exercise we go on breathing hard and the heart beats fast: extra oxygen is needed to break down the lactic acid. This extra oxygen is called the **oxygen debt**.

blocks.caption: Yeast fermentation produces carbon dioxide.
blocks.alt: A flask of yeast and glucose joined by a delivery tube to a tube of limewater, which turns milky.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Respiration is *not* breathing, and it is not the same as photosynthesis.
- Plants respire all the time, not only at night.
- Anaerobic respiration releases some energy; it does not release none.
- Energy is *released* from glucose, it is not 'made'.

blocks.title: Rate of fermentation
blocks.statement: Yeast in warm sugar solution gives 24 bubbles of gas in 2 minutes at 20 °C, and 54 bubbles in 2 minutes at 35 °C. Calculate the rates in bubbles per minute.
steps: Enzymes work faster at the warmer temperature (below the optimum).

blocks.title: After a 100 m race
blocks.statement: A boy runs the 100 m race in Bamenda and keeps breathing hard for several minutes. Explain.
steps: His muscles respired partly anaerobically and made lactic acid.
He needs extra oxygen to break the lactic acid down: he repays the oxygen debt by deep, fast breathing.
blocks.answer: To repay the oxygen debt and remove lactic acid.
